claims.text: The tested material is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate.
Overall wear resistance is primarily governed by the coating's high-temperature microstructural stability.
Microscopic deformation during sliding is primarily governed by the coating's high-temperature microstructural stability.
Changing alloy composition to increase the proportion of solid-solution-strengthening phases will enhance microstructural stability.
An increased proportion of solid-solution-strengthening phases enhances load-bearing capacity.
An increased proportion of solid-solution-strengthening phases increases resistance to dislocation movement.
Enhanced load-bearing capacity and resistance to dislocation movement will improve wear resistance.
Enhanced load-bearing capacity and resistance to dislocation movement will reduce microscopic deformation.
The compositionally modified coating will have greater wear resistance than the baseline coating.
The compositionally modified coating will exhibit less microscopic deformation than the baseline coating.
The predictions are limited to a high-temperature sliding regime in which significant microstructural changes occur.
The composition changes needed for optimal performance and the magnitudes of the wear and deformation improvements are uncertain.
